main_body: Thatched hut: a large sloped thatch roof (rows ~4-53) over a log-plank wall with a central door and two round shields (rows ~53-78), on a stone base strip
top_band: Golden thatch roof slope, rows ~4-52, lightest ochre at the top with darker course lines. It ends in a lighter eave band at ~rows 49-53 over a dark shadow line.
evidence: Same construction as the Beodeul reference houses. A big roof slope reads as the top surface (thatch courses, lighter eave edge at ~row 52). Below it is a darker log-wall front face, with a shadow strip directly under the eave. The door has a timber frame, a dark inner edge and a dark interior, so it reads as inset. A stone base runs along the bottom. No receding side faces.

style.evidence: The thatch has about 5 ochre steps, with a per-course highlight, dark course lines and speckle. The log wall has vertical grain in several browns. The outlines are dark brown and dark ochre rather than black. The round shields, bone skull and stone base add variety. It sits comfortably next to the reference houses and does not look flat or sticker-like. The dark door interior is the only large flat area, and it is small.
